items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: Billie Holiday’s voice on “Lady in Satin,” was, not really so great anymore, and yet it’s the most moving record that I’ve ever heard by a singer, to me.

ctx.x: What always fascinated me, more than the guys that could play and run a lot of changes, is the guys who could play a melody, kind of like a singer, and move people. Or play very simply and move people. That’s the mysterious part to me. Because I always said if I heard somebody play a whole bunch of notes, oh wow, he can do that and I can’t do that. Or wow, boy I’d have to practice to be able to do that. But when you hear Frank Sinatra sing or you hear Louis Armstrong play some simple solo, not his tough ones,…
Were you affected by the rock ‘n roll scene that was forming at the time also?
